item.title: 第二季度南非经济收缩,被伊朗战争拖下水
item.author: By Kopano Gumbi
item.description:
本地机器翻译 · 原文附后

由克帕诺·贡比(英语:Kopano Gumbi)出品.

PRETORIA, 9月8日(路透社) - 南非经济在2026年第二季度近两年来首次萎缩,

• 国内生产总值按季度季度调整后收缩0.2%。

路透社调查的经济学家预测会收缩0.1%.

更多来自雅虎童子军

哪个部门推动了南非国内生产总值的下降?

经济学家对2026年增长的预测是什么?.

伊朗战争如何影响南非经济?.

是什么导致南非在Q2经济收缩?.

• 收缩主要是由于采矿(-3.0%)、制造业(-1.8%)和贸易(-1.9%)部门的产出下降所驱动的。

• “中东的局势确实反映在这些数字中。

南非统计局经济统计负责人Joe de Beer表示,

• 他补充了第三季度数据,以确定2026年的年增长率能否战胜经济学家目前1.2%到1.5%的预测。

• 在2月下旬伊朗战争开始之前,财政部今年的目标是1.6%的增长,但国内燃料价格上涨使前景暗淡。

非洲首席经济学家拉齐亚·汗(Razia Khan)在《标准宪章》上发表电子邮件评论,

• 家庭支出是南非经济的主要驱动力,第二季度仍在积极地区,尽管固定投资再次下降。

——展望第三季度,西北大学商学院经济学家雷蒙德·帕森斯(英语:Raymond Parsons)教授说:"有证据表明,在经济中,复苏已经被中断并被推迟,而不是被确定为脱轨".

(由克帕诺·贡比报告;由斯富多·帕拉科佐夫、尼卢特帕尔·蒂姆西纳和阿纳蒂·马杜贝拉补充报告;由亚历山大·温宁和休·劳森编辑)

原文：South African economy shrinks in second quarter, dragged down by Iran war

By Kopano Gumbi

PRETORIA, Sept 8 (Reuters) - South Africa's economy shrank for the first time in almost two years in ‌the second quarter of 2026, official data showed on Tuesday, ‌as the Iran war depressed domestic demand and the mining and manufacturing sectors performed poorly.

• Gross domestic product contracted 0.2% on a seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.1% contraction.

What caused South Africa's economic contraction in Q2?

• The contraction was mainly driven by output falls in the mining (-3.0%), manufacturing (-1.8%) and ‌trade (-1.9%) sectors.

• "The situation in ⁠the Middle East definitely reflected in these numbers. The question we don't yet know is how long this ⁠will persist, especially for manufacturing," said Joe de Beer, head of economic statistics at Statistics South Africa.

• He added third-quarter data would determine whether 2026's annual growth rate could beat economists' current projections of 1.2% ‌to 1.5%.

• Before the Iran war started in late February, the finance ministry was targeting 1.6% growth this year, but domestic fuel price hikes have since darkened the outlook.

• "Higher fuel prices clearly hit demand in South Africa really hard," Razia Khan, chief Africa economist at ‌Standard Chartered, said in emailed comments.

• Household spending is a key driver of the South African economy and remained in positive territory in the second quarter, ‌though fixed investments fell again.

• Looking ahead to the third quarter, North-West University Business School economist Prof Raymond Parsons said: "The evidence points to an economy in which recovery has been interrupted and ‌delayed, rather than definitively derailed."

(Reporting by Kopano Gumbi; Addditional reporting by Sfundo Parakozov, Nilutpal Timsina and Anathi Madubela; Editing by Alexander Winning and Hugh Lawson)
